reason.river: Snow in the {basin} basin is {levelText}; {cropLower} needs about {need} m³ and the field can expect about {supply} m³.
reason.well: Water comes from a well, so the snow signal does not change this answer; {cropLower} needs about {need} m³ and the well gives about {supply} m³.
reason.rain: Rain only: useful rain gives about {supply} m³, while {cropLower} needs about {need} m³ more.

verdict.season: Snow value: February–March {year}. This is a risk signal, not a forecast.

alt.title: Other options · your priority: {priority}
alt.none: No other crop can grow on this field this season.

tip.cereal: After a cereal, a legume such as chickpea or beans restores nitrogen.
tip.legume: After a legume, nitrogen stays in the soil: barley or maize will do well.
tip.root: After potato or beet, sow a cereal to break the disease cycle.
tip.oilseed: Sow sunflower on the same field only once in 6–7 years; follow it with a cereal or a legume.
tip.fodder: After alfalfa, maize or a cereal makes good use of the nitrogen it leaves.

evidence.title: What this answer is based on
evidence.soilInfo: Soil: {soil}. Shown for information only, not used in the calculation.
evidence.formula: Need = (crop need − 0.7 × rain) × 10 × ha. Supply = 9,717 m³/ha × ha × snow × 0.82 × 0.6. Fit = supply ÷ need: ≥1.1 enough, 0.9–1.1 tight, <0.9 short.
evidence.notForecast: The snow signal is a risk label, never a forecast. In published Naryn studies snow explains about 60% of seasonal flow; glaciers (up to half of July–August flow) and summer rain explain the rest.

about.intro: iSEED turns NASA satellite snow data into a seasonal water-risk signal for each river basin in Kyrgyzstan.
about.missNote: Shortage years the signal misses are shown too: glacier melt and summer heat explain them.
about.seasonNote: It is November: next season's snow has not fallen yet. The app shows the last full season (February–March 2026) as the worked example, and snow so far this winter as an early signal.
about.demoNote: In this prototype the snow, basin, climate and income numbers are demo data. The real values are computed by the scripts in scripts/ during the event.

src.modis: NASA MODIS MOD10A1 v6.1: daily snow cover, 500 m. NASA open data.
src.power: NASA POWER (AG): temperature, rain, soil wetness. Free, cite NASA POWER.
src.basins: HydroBASINS level 5 (HydroSHEDS): basin boundaries. Free with attribution.
src.fao: FAO-56 (Tables 11, 12) and the FAO Crop Calendar for Kyrgyzstan: crop water need.
src.stats: National statistics: 6.19 km³ irrigation water (2024), ≈637,000 ha irrigated, 1.7–2.3 km³ losses.
src.tiles: Esri World Imagery and OpenStreetMap (ODbL): the map. Photon (OpenStreetMap data): place search.
src.border: geoBoundaries (OpenStreetMap, ODbL): the border of Kyrgyzstan. Lakes and reservoirs: OpenStreetMap (ODbL).
src.elevation: Open-Meteo Elevation API (Copernicus DEM, 90 m): height of the spot, fields above 3,000 m are refused.
